clue.text: Seasoned sausage with starters of stuffed aubergines lures friend in Paris

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: the first letters of three words
the French word for a friend

explanation.surface: A cook stuffs aubergines with spicy sausage to tempt a French friend to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a recipe, but only the initials of three words are needed before the French friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly spiced Italian sausage, so it is a classic example of a seasoned one.

clue.text: Lout in a mob rampaging is individually exposed

indicators.note: a rampaging crowd runs wild and out of order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A yob caught up in a rioting crowd finds himself exposed when he is singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'Lout in a mob' supplies the letters; the rampaging mob is the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in a risky position with no support from others, alone and vulnerable.

clue.text: Play featuring titled figure generally marginalised by holy books

indicators.note: the margins are the edges, so only the outside letters of the word survive

blocks.note: a peer holds a title such as lord or earl
the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A drama whose aristocratic character is usually sidelined by religious scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' looks like an adverb meaning usually, but its edges are taken. NT for New Testament is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer Gynt is the verse drama by Henrik Ibsen, famous also for Grieg's incidental music.

clue.text: Agents following in this way Liberal Party

indicators.note: coming after something else, so this group of letters is placed behind the previous one

explanation.surface: Spies tag along behind the Liberal Party, as political surveillance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Party' looks like one political name, but Liberal is just L and Party is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a friendly gathering held by a club or group, an informal kind of celebration.

clue.text: Ring before work on board ship to get seafood

indicators.note: placed in front, so this group precedes the next one
to be on board a vessel is to be inside it, so letters go within

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A sailor phones ahead before starting his shift aboard a ship to order shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: SS for steamship is the container; the call and the opus sit inside it, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are bivalve shellfish with fan-shaped shells, widely eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Firm with a spell in trouble has to fold

indicators.note: something in trouble is in a mess, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A company that goes through a bad patch has to shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' is a business going under, which the surface sets up neatly; 'with' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold, of a business, is to fail and close, which is the same as to collapse.

clue.text: North Warwickshire town where sister misplaced a note  …

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: In a Midlands town a nun has lost a letter or banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a market town in Warwickshire, central England. The ellipsis hands 'a note' on to the next clue as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuneaton lies in the north of the English county of Warwickshire, near Coventry.

clue.text: Neighbour set up brass instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up turns it bottom to top

blocks.note: as a verb, to neighbour is to border on

explanation.surface: The person next door has set up a large brass horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' is read as a noun in the surface but is a verb meaning to adjoin.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the largest and lowest-pitched member of the brass family of instruments.

clue.text: Requirement for work in a bakery, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: bakers work dough with their hands

explanation.surface: A job requirement for anyone working in a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K means the baker's verb and the answer sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something necessary, so it is a straightforward synonym for something required.

clue.text: …  covering round character with enough money to keep going

definitions.text: with enough money to keep going

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around, so the outer letters wrap the inner ones

blocks.note: the ellipsis carries over 'a note' from the previous clue, read as the musical note A flat
the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Following on, a note covers a round-faced character who has just enough cash to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis borrows 'a note' from the previous clue: here it is A FLAT, a musical note, which goes around the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that stays afloat is solvent, with sufficient funds to continue trading, a common figurative idiom.

clue.text: Dreadful dump entered by two bishops touring island

indicators.note: a place entered by someone has them inside it
a tour goes all the way around a place, so letters encircle others

blocks.note: a dump is a squalid place, a hole
RR for Right Reverend and B for bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: Two clergymen on a tour of an island find a dismal dump.
explanation.walkthrough: The two bishops are different abbreviations: RR (Right Reverend) and B (chess); they straddle I and then sit inside the dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful and horrible are near synonyms, both meaning very unpleasant or terrible.

clue.text: Top actress gained ally in play about drama's opening

indicators.note: letters at play move freely and so land in a new order
to be about something is to surround it
an opening is the start, so only the first letter is kept

explanation.surface: A star actress finds a friend among the cast of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' sounds theatrical, which suits the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange; the rearranged letters wrap the first letter of drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading lady takes the principal female role in a production, so she is the top actress.

clue.text: Staple Western character nursing leg when shot

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A typical cowboy in a film tends his leg after being shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' fits the Western scene perfectly as gunfire, but it signals that the letters are wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed gunfighter is a stock figure of cowboy films and novels set in the American frontier.

clue.text: Clear set of policy proposals with nothing eliminated

indicators.note: something eliminated is removed, so letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A political programme set out plainly with no ideas thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The election document loses its final O, nothing, to leave the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means plain or obvious to see, a synonym of evident and clear.

clue.text: Flood in a French department at the end of June

indicators.note: the end is the last part, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the French masculine word for a

explanation.surface: A French administrative region is hit by summer floods late in June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French department' looks like one phrase naming a region of France, but 'a French' is UN and department is just D.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, so it is a verb synonym of flood.

clue.text: License first person at work showing enthusiastic interest

blocks.note: a machine at work is on

explanation.surface: A licensed worker, the first at the office, shows real zeal for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'License' is a noun here, a permit, not the verb to authorise.
explanation.definitionFit: A passion is a strong liking or enthusiasm for an activity, such as a hobby.

clue.text: Episode going wrong in end? It encapsulates Conservative

indicators.note: things going wrong fall out of order, so the letters are rearranged
a capsule holds something inside it

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political episode that goes badly at the end involves the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface into two sentences, but 'in end? It' is one stretch of letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is a single event or occurrence, as is an episode in a sequence of happenings.

clue.text: Progressing like a rail passenger?

blocks.note: surface reading: advancing on a journey, as a traveller does
setter's reading: a passenger is literally seated inside a carriage, while the phrase also means under way

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning 'under way' is read literally as where a railway traveller sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in train are in progress, already set in motion, which is a slightly formal idiom.

clue.text: Star is given fixed allowance for festivity

explanation.surface: A famous person receives a set budget to throw a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous person and the allowance sit side by side to build the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: A festivity is a joyful occasion or party, the same thing as a celebration.

clue.text: Wading bird fluttering at cove

indicators.note: something fluttering flaps about restlessly, so its letters move position

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shorebird flaps its wings at a small bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluttering' fits a bird perfectly, which hides its role as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white shorebird with an upturned bill that feeds in shallow water.

clue.text: A country once losing money — or a number of countries

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so letters are dropped

explanation.surface: A nation that used to be wealthy goes broke, or perhaps several nations do.
explanation.walkthrough: SIAM was Thailand's name until 1939; drop its M for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is a continent, so it contains many separate nations, a playfully vague description.

clue.text: Disorder found in room, essentially

blocks.note: second meaning: a room where members of the armed forces eat together

explanation.surface: An untidy room is, at heart, chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the messy bedroom; the second sense is the military dining room, as in an officers' mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a disordered state and a communal dining hall for service personnel.

clue.text: Parking in beginning in front of garage— it's an offence

indicators.note: something put in another thing sits inside it
the front is the leading part, so only the first letter is kept
placed ahead, so the earlier pieces come before the next

blocks.note: a seed is the origin of something

explanation.surface: Parking at the start of a driveway outside a garage is against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The parking sign P sits inside the seed, the beginning, then IN and the garage's first letter follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving over the speed limit is a motoring crime, so speeding is a specific traffic offence.

clue.text: Person in familiar sense, say, associated with a wine shop

blocks.note: bod is informal British slang for a person

explanation.surface: Someone's intuitive feel is linked to running an off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In familiar sense' just marks the next word as slang: a bod is a person in casual British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or shop selling wine, and in the US a small grocery.

clue.text: One missing a book dispatched by European conglomerate, finally

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the end, so only the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A book sent out by a big European company has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: A string of short pieces: the article, the book abbreviation, a past tense, then two E's from different sources.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present where expected, such as at work or school.

clue.text: Establish residence in US city overlooking eastern tip of Florida

indicators.note: to overlook something is to leave it out
in an across clue the east is the right-hand end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone sets up home in an American city with a view over the Florida coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern tip of Florida' sounds like geography, as if the Keys or Miami, but it means the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle somewhere is to make a permanent home there, to take up residence.
